item.title: Functional limit theorems for weighted occupation times of supercritical superprocesses
item.description: arXiv:2610.12503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a supercritical superprocess with a non-local branching mechanism on a Lusin space $E$, whose mean semigroup admits a positive leading eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ with a bounded positive eigenfunction $\varphi$ and a finite eigenmeasure $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Let $Y_t:=\int_0^t X_s\mathrm{d}s$ be its occupation measure. We first prove a law of large numbers, that is, for every bounded measurable function $f$, $e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ converges in $L^2$ to $\lambda_1^{-1}\langle f,\widetilde{\varphi}\rangle W^\varphi_\infty$, where $W^\varphi_\infty$ is the limit of the martingale $W^\varphi_t:=e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle\varphi,X_t\rangle$. We then establish functional central limit theorems for the fluctuations of $\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ around this random centering. We show that the normalisation and the limit are determined by the spectral decay rate of $f$ compared with the critical value $\lambda_1/2$, and there are three possible regimes: after suitable normalisation, the fluctuation process converges in distribution in $\mathcal{C}[0,+\infty)$ either to a mixed Gaussian process $\sqrt{W^{\varphi}_{\infty}}G(f)$, or to a constant Gaussian process with random variance depending on $W^{\varphi}_{\infty}$, or to a non-Gaussian limit given by the limit of a martingale associated with the spectral projection of $f$. These results are the occupation-time counterparts of the fluctuation theorems for linear functionals of supercritical non-local branching superprocesses.
item.dc:creator: Ting Yang

item.title: Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.12589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_\delta$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.
item.dc:creator: Yaohui Lin, Tiankui Lu

item.title: Stochastic Modelling of Telomere Length Dynamics During Hematopoiesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.12660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new stochastic model of telomere length dynamics during hematopoiesis. The numerous cell divisions occurring in this setting makes telomere length dynamics, and in particular their attrition, a crucial aspect of hematopoiesis. After recalling the main aspect of the biological setting, we describe an individual based model of hematopoietic population cells. We then study its behaviour in the large population limit, as well as its fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Sophie Baland, Simon Toupance, Denis Villemonais

item.title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.12722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent, not necessarily identically distributed, random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\). Let \(S_n\) denote the sum, let \(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\), and let \(G\sim N(0,\Sigma)\). Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma}{\|\Sigma\|}, \qquad v(\Sigma)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)}{\|\Sigma\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions \(r(\Sigma)\le C_\Sigma v(\Sigma)\) and \(v(\Sigma)\ge6\), we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(\Sigma)^{3/2}}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the fixed parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The bound is uniform at the endpoint \(v(\Sigma)=6\), without a logarithmic loss. Its main feature is the combination of the \(n^{-1}\) rate with dependence on effective rank, including this endpoint. Consequently, the bound can vanish when \(r(\Sigma)=o(n^{2/3})\), even when \(p\) is much larger than \(n\). The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof builds on the Fourier and symmetrization methods of \citet{GoetzeZaitsev2014}, combined with moment matching, truncation, and comparison estimates that retain the covariance structure.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Naumov, Sergey Samsonov, Vladimir Spokoiny, Vladimir Ulyanov

item.title: Large deviations for additive functionals of one-dimensional zero-range processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.12814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a large deviation principle for additive functionals of local Lipschitz functions of a one-dimensional symmetric zero-range process on the diffusive scale. The rate function is obtained from the dynamical large deviation principle for the empirical density and is characterized by a variational constraint involving the density at a fixed spatial point. On the microscopic side, a super-exponential replacement is needed to replace the local observable with a function of the empirical density. On the macroscopic side, the spatial regularity enjoyed by finite-rate trajectories is needed to pass from spatial averages to point evaluation.
item.dc:creator: Insuk Seo, Kenkichi Tsunoda

item.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.12950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.
item.dc:creator: Christian Houdr\'e, Dorian Kidonakis

item.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.
item.dc:creator: Hugh Zheng

item.title: Penalizations of Two-Dimensional Simple Random Walk by Direction-Dependent Excursion Counts and Edge-Crossing Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.13069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study penalizations of the two-dimensional simple random walk by functions of direction-dependent excursion counts and edge-crossing counts. The former record completed excursions with prescribed pairs of departure and return directions at the origin, whereas the latter record crossings of a prescribed set of unoriented edges incident to the origin. We determine the distributions of their almost surely finite terminal values and derive explicit path decomposition formulas involving the random walk conditioned to avoid the origin. Moreover, both families of penalized measures can be represented by weighting and normalizing the same universal $\sigma$-finite measure associated with local-time penalization at the origin. Thus, direction-dependent excursion counts, edge-crossing counts, and local time at the origin give rise to penalizations belonging to a common universality class.
item.dc:creator: Syota Esaki, Kohki Iba

item.title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.13266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.
item.dc:creator: Zdzislaw Brzezniak, Benedetta Ferrario, Margherita Zanella

item.title: Time-changed reflected diffusions: subdiffusion, superdiffusion and explosion
item.description: arXiv:2610.13302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by semi-Markov models of anomalous diffusion, we study obliquely reflected diffusions in generalized parabolic domains under independent inverse-subordinator time changes. We focus on infinite-mean subordinators, whose inverse clocks can slow the superdiffusive growth induced by reflection. For domains with cross-sectional radius asymptotic to $a_\infty x^\beta$, where $-1<\beta<1$, we strengthen the almost-sure growth laws of [MMW23] to obtain precise second-moment asymptotics when the subordinator's Laplace exponent is regularly varying at zero, and matching bounds more generally. Inverse $\alpha$-stable clocks yield mean-square growth of order $t^{2\alpha/(1+\beta)}$, giving subdiffusive, diffusive, or superdiffusive regimes. For $\beta<-1$, explosion persists almost surely, with finite mean explosion time if and only if the subordinator has finite mean. Supporting results establish strong existence, pathwise uniqueness, and a time-change representation, also allowing dependent clocks.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Francesco Virgili

item.title: Higher-Order Gaussian Approximations on Path Space for the Simple Symmetric Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.13308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantitative Gaussian approximation estimates on path space are established for the nonequilibrium density fluctuations of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) on a $d$-dimensional discrete torus of mesh size $1/n$, started from a product measure with a smooth density profile. A novel $n$-dependent modified Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is constructed that incorporates higher-order lattice information while remaining linear and Gaussian. It is shown that, for sufficiently high modification orders, this modification yields quantitative Gaussian approximation error bounds of order $n^{-\min\{d/2,2\}}$ for a class of smooth functionals of the entire fluctuation trajectory. In addition, it is shown that retaining an explicit microscopic correlation correction leaves a remainder of order $n^{-d/2}$, thereby distinguishing contributions to the bound due to correlations from those due to spatial approximation. For nonconstant initial profiles in dimensions $d\ge3$, a separate argument yields matching upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-2}$ for the direct weak error of suitable quadratic test functionals, provided that the modification orders are sufficiently high. The proof is based on a novel path-dependent Trotter formula. Its derivation builds on the introduction of a concept of horizontal absolute continuity for non-anticipative functionals and a corresponding martingale formula for Markov jump processes. This formula is subsequently combined with an integral backward Kolmogorov equation for Gaussian continuation functionals. A second ingredient of the proof is a refinement of the exchangeable-pair argument introduced by the authors in a previous work, thereby improving the central-limit rate $n^{-\min\{d/2,1\}}$ to $n^{-d/2}$ for the initial empirical fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Gess, Vitalii Konarovskyi

item.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part~1: expectation under the uniform null
item.description: arXiv:2610.13366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the expectation of the discrete total variation statistic $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$ of counts $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $n$ ordered bins with sample size $N$, under the uniform multinomial null. In the notation used throughout the series, a reference distribution $\mathbf r$ defines $d_{\mathbf r}(x)=\|x-N\mathbf r\|_V$; here $\mathbf r=\mathbf u$ is uniform and we write simply $d$. We obtain an exact single-sum formula, a closed form in central trinomial coefficients valid for every $n\ge2$, with one-term evaluations at $n=2,4$ and a complete D-finite characterization for $n=3$. The per-edge expectation $W_N=E|X_2-X_1|$ satisfies an exact three-term recurrence, from which we derive its complete $1/N$ expansion with the $n$-independent constant $E(d^\circ/\sqrt{Nn})\to 2/\sqrt\pi$ for the cyclic statistic $d^\circ=d^\circ_{\mathbf u}$, independent of the number of bins; the complementary sparse regime (fixed $N$, $n\to\infty$) is treated in a separate paper. Conditioning on a two-bin total reduces each edge to a symmetric random walk; as the subsequent parts of the series will show, this method carries the analysis to non-uniform reference laws.
item.dc:creator: N. Bani\'c, N. Elezovi\'c

item.title: BKT transition for $\mathsf{Sine}_\beta$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase transition in the large-distance behaviour of the two-point correlation function of the $\mathsf{Sine}_\beta$ point process for all $\beta>0$, confirming the first term of an asymptotic expansion predicted by Forrester.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Assiotis

item.title: On the weak invariance principle for strictly stationary sequences in some Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the weak invariance principle in some Besov spaces for strictly stationary sequences. In particular, we provide sufficient conditions on the moments and the dependence of a strictly stationary sequence to guaranty the weak invariance principle in these Besov spaces. Several dependence structures are considered, including projective conditions, $\alpha$-dependent, $\rho$-mixing, and $\tau$ -dependent conditions. The main tools in the proofs are martingale approximation and deviation inequalities for weakly dependent sequences. Our results cover a large range of strictly stationary sequences that were not treated previously in the literature. Moreover, the presented conditions are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Davide Giraudo (IRMA, UNISTRA UFR MI), Sadillo Sharipov

item.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
item.description: arXiv:2610.13531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.
item.dc:creator: Charaf Bellourak (LJK, DAO), Sylvain Meignen (LJK, DAO), K\'evin Polisano (LJK, SVH), Micka\"el Nahon (LJK)

item.title: An infinite-dimensional representation of Ray-Knight theorems for the Bass-Burdzy flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.13561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: [Bass and Burdzy 1999] introduced a stochastic flow of homeomorphisms of the real line $\mathcal R_t:x\mapsto \mathcal R_t(x)$, driven by a Brownian motion. Ray-Knight theorems for the process $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$ were later obtained by [Hu and Warren 2000]. We extend their results by proving an integral representation driven by a common white noise for the local times of $\mathcal R_t^{-1}(0)$, in analogy with the case of the standard Ray-Knight theorems [A\"id\'ekon, Hu and Shi 2024]. We generalize this representation to the setting of a Bass-Burdzy flow driven by a drifted Brownian motion perturbed at its maximum, and use this framework to answer a question of [A\"id\'ekon, Hu and Shi 2026] concerning the description of the conditional law of a perturbed reflecting Brownian motion given its occupation measure in terms of Bass-Burdzy flows.
item.dc:creator: Chengshi Wang

item.title: Metastable confinement of particle systems near linearly stable McKean-Vlasov equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.13655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general metastability principle showing that the local stability of a McKean-Vlasov equilibrium implies exponentially long confinement of the associated particle system. Consider interacting diffusions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a general smooth and bounded interaction kernel and a globally Lipschitz drift that is dissipative at large distances. Assume the McKean-Vlasov equation has at least one equilibrium which is locally exponentially stable. We prove that the probability that the empirical measure leaves a sufficiently small fixed Wasserstein-1 neighborhood of the selected equilibrium before time $T$ is bounded by $C(1+T)e^{-cN}$, where $N$ is the number of particles and $C,c>0$ are independent of $N$ and $T$. Consequently, confinement holds up to times $e^{\gamma N}$, for every $0<\gamma<c$, with exponentially small exit probability. The proof combines an explicit Volterra construction of the linearized Fokker-Planck semigroup, a mild representation of empirical fluctuations, and exponential maximal estimates for stochastic convolutions. Our approach does not require a gradient flow structure or reversibility of the equations.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Chan-ashing, Quentin Cormier

item.title: Conditioning diffusions on a terminal bearing
item.description: arXiv:2610.13659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sampling of a diffusion on $[0,T]$ conditioned on its terminal position lying on a prescribed ray, i.e. on an exactly observed bearing. For a linear drift we derive closed-form expressions for the Doob $h$-function and its gradient. For a broad class of tracking models admitting a Kronecker block structure, the guiding term is obtained from a single row of a matrix exponential, and the conditioned process decomposes into independent radial and angular components. For a nonlinear drift, we construct a guided process using the $h$-function of the linear model and prove absolute continuity of the law of the true conditioned process with respect to the law of the guided process, with an explicit likelihood ratio. This result is used to devise an auxiliary particle filter for bearings observed sequentially in time without noise. Numerical experiments show that the proposed filter approximates the filtering distribution and estimates the log-likelihood considerably more accurately than the shifted Rayleigh filter, at the cost of a higher computing time.
item.dc:creator: Frank van der Meulen

item.title: TAP variational formula for 2-spin models with general interaction matrix and marginality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Thouless--Anderson--Palmer (TAP) variational formula for the free energy of spherical $2$-spin models whose interaction matrices have a compactly supported limiting spectral distribution. The formula holds at every inverse temperature and, in particular, extends the TAP representation previously obtained for the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main contribution is a new microcanonical proof designed to handle marginality. We partition the sphere according to the smallest collection of top eigendirections carrying a prescribed fraction of the norm. On every element of this partition, the remaining degrees of freedom are effectively at high temperature and their contribution can be computed through spherical-integral asymptotics. The resulting auxiliary variational problem separates the macroscopic low-temperature contribution from the high-temperature fluctuation term; its maximization recovers the usual TAP functional and Plefka condition. This decomposition also shows why neighborhoods of the TAP maximizers alone do not capture the Gibbs mass: all eigendirections associated with large eigenvalues contribute on the same exponential scale, a manifestation of the marginality of spherical $2$-spin states.
item.dc:creator: David Belius, Simon Briend, Volodymyr Fomichov

item.title: Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = \theta\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + \sigma\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(\theta>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(\sigma>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=\psi+R\) with \(\psi\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and H\"older in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(\psi\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(\psi\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(\Omega)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(\theta\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an It\^o process.
item.dc:creator: Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor

item.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
item.description: arXiv:2610.13800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^\alpha\,dW_t$, $0 < \alpha < 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-\alpha)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $\Theta_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $\Theta_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $\Theta_h \to \theta \in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $\theta/|\log\alpha|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $\Theta_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Tanaka

item.title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.13836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.
item.dc:creator: Egor Kosov

item.title: Interacting Stochastic Systems with Agent-Based Sampling and Connection-Based Reinforcement
item.description: arXiv:2610.13884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a general class of interacting reinforced stochastic systems evolving on a network. The dynamics are governed by two distinct interaction structures: a sampling network, which determines how information is acquired, and a reinforcement network, which determines how the sampled information influences future evolution. Processes generate Bernoulli observations through preferential, de-preferential, or mixed sampling, while observations are transmitted through an edge-dependent affine reinforcement mechanism. We formulate the dynamics as a stochastic approximation scheme and study their asymptotic behaviour. We establish sufficient conditions for almost sure convergence to a deterministic limit and, when the sampling and reinforcement graphs coincide, derive graph-theoretic criteria involving odd cycles, mixed-sampling vertices, and subcritical reinforcement. Under additional structural assumptions, we establish almost sure convergence and partial synchronization in a random-limit regime. In the deterministic regime, we also prove a law of the iterated logarithm and a central limit theorem under suitable spectral and regularity conditions. Finally, we show how the framework encompasses interacting urn models with edge-dependent reinforcement, urns with memory, and random walks with memory.
item.dc:creator: Yogesh Dahiya, Gursharn Kaur, Neeraja Sahasrabudhe

item.title: Markov Chain Convergence in Kernel-Induced Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.13916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the convergence of Markov chains in the geometry induced by Hilbertian embeddings associated with positive definite kernels, also called Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). Under a contraction assumption in the kernel-induced geometry, and a standard spectral gap assumption, we establish non-asymptotic, high-probability bounds for the convergence of the empirical occupation measure to the invariant measure. The obtained bounds separate the roles of the two conditions: the spectral gap determines the effective sample size in the leading term, while the kernel contraction enters only through a linear correction. As an application, we study one-step prediction of dynamical systems from a single trajectory, deriving fast learning rates for a nonlinear least-squares estimator. The rates highlight the interplay between mixing properties in the kernel-induced geometry and the classical source and capacity conditions used in the analysis of least-squares.
item.dc:creator: Oleksii Kachaiev, Luc Brogat-Motte, Silvia Villa, Lorenzo Rosasco

item.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
item.description: arXiv:2610.13940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-L,L]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain, and Athreya and J\'arai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $L\to\infty$. By a formula of Dhar (1990), when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the expected number of topplings at a site in the resulting avalanche is proportional to the Green function of simple random walk from the origin. This Green function is finite for $d\geq3$, where J\'arai and Redig (2008) proved that avalanches are almost surely finite, and infinite for $d=2$. We prove that for $d=2$ avalanches are nevertheless almost surely finite: the probability that an avalanche reaches distance $R$ is at most a negative power of $\log R$. The proof follows the avalanche backward and reduces the question to an estimate for the uniform spanning tree, which we prove by a multiscale electrical argument.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bou-Rabee

item.title: A Second-Order Asymptotic Expansion for Nonlinear Filtering in the Lorenz--63 System
item.description: arXiv:2610.12512v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A challenge in nonlinear filtering is to incorporate nonlinear effects into approximations of the conditional mean while retaining a finite-dimensional recursive algorithm. We derive a second-order asymptotic expansion of the filtering mean with respect to the system-noise intensity. We apply this expansion to the Lorenz--63 model, a prototypical three-dimensional chaotic dynamical system. The first-order approximation is computed using a Kalman--Bucy filter for the system linearized around the deterministic reference trajectory. The second-order correction incorporates the Hessian of the Lorenz--63 drift and is computed through a closed recursive system with 3+9+18=30 independent scalar components. The full system, including the reference trajectory and the first-order mean and covariance, has 42 independent scalar components. To support stable tracking of chaotic trajectories over long time intervals, we introduce recentering of the expansion and redistribution of Gaussian components between expansion orders. In the numerical experiments, we compare the proposed algorithm with an ensemble transform Kalman filter (ETKF) as a practical benchmark and a particle filter (PF) as a numerical reference. Under the full-observation settings, the proposed algorithm achieves a lower root-mean-square error relative to the truth and a smaller distance to the 10,000-particle PF reference than the 20-member ETKF. These results suggest that the proposed second-order extension of Kalman filtering has the potential to balance filtering accuracy and computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Masahiro Kurisaki, Kota Takeda

item.title: Tandem Queues with Hybrid Abandonment in Heavy Traffic
item.description: arXiv:2610.12716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid-abandonment systems, where jobs abandon from certain stages of service but not others, occur frequently in medical, service, and computing systems. Abandonment affects the heavy-traffic behavior of both the stages with and without abandonment. In contrast to existing heavy-traffic works that focus on cases where there is abandonment at either all stages or no stages, we focus on the heavy-traffic behavior for these hybrid-abandonment systems. We provide the first heavy-traffic characterization of the second queue length in a two-stage tandem queue with abandonment only in the first stage. We characterize the scaled mean of the second stage queue length and prove that the scaled second queue length is asymptotically exponentially distributed and asymptotically independent of the first stage queue length. We derive our results by analyzing Markovian arrival process queues with countably infinite phases. We do this by extending techniques used to analyze queues with Markov-modulated arrivals to the broader class of infinite Markovian arrival process queues. We prove asymptotic results for a more general infinite phase process condition, an infinite birth-death phase process, and the hybrid-abandonment tandem case. We also empirically demonstrate that our heavy-traffic approximations are good approximations across various system settings.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Curtis, Izzy Grosof, Seyed Iravani

item.title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
item.description: arXiv:2610.12765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$. For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.
item.dc:creator: Dong Huang, Shuangping Li

item.title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.
item.dc:creator: Vivek Khatana, Aditya Gahlawat, Naira Hovakimyan, Petros Voulgaris

item.title: An efficient stochastic generalized method of moments estimator for nonlinear moment models
item.description: arXiv:2610.12873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic properties of the nonlinear stochastic GMM algorithm proposed by Chen, Lee, Liao, Seo, Shin and Song for recursively estimating parameters defined by possibly nonlinear and overidentified moment restrictions $\E[g(X,\beta^*)]=0$. Each observation updates estimates of the moment Jacobian, inverse covariance matrix and Gauss--Newton preconditioner at a cost independent of sample size. For linear and nonlinear instrumental-variable moments, we derive an exact rank-two Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury update. The algorithm combines preconditioned stochastic approximation with iterate averaging. Under a preconditioned monotonicity condition, satisfied globally in linear models and locally around a consistent pilot estimate in general, we establish almost sure convergence and rates, as well as a functional central limit theorem with the efficient GMM variance. These results require four moments of the moment function and its Jacobian when the step exponent exceeds $2/3$. The inverse Gauss--Newton matrix consistently estimates this variance, and a projected linearised statistic enables online testing of overidentifying restrictions. We extend the results to $L$-dependent data with long-run variance weights under stronger moment assumptions. Simulations show that the averaged estimator approaches offline two-step GMM in accuracy and coverage at $10^6$ observations, while requiring a fraction of its computing time and fixed memory at up to $10^7$ observations. The online test achieves correct size and comparable power. In an application estimating the effect of a third child on weeks worked using $254{,}654$ women from the 1980 US Census, single-pass estimates agree with offline GMM within a fraction of a standard error on average across data orderings, and both methods yield the same overidentification-test conclusion in most orderings.
item.dc:creator: Duy Nguyen

item.title: On the composition of permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.12945v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators. We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs. As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gorski

item.title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.12949v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Weighted derivative estimates for Kolmogorov equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For diffusions whose coefficients are smooth, with at most linear growth and bounded derivatives of higher order, we establish explicit pointwise bounds on the spatial derivatives of the classical solution to the Cauchy problem with polynomially growing initial data. We also obtain explicit growth estimates for the derivatives of the SDE with respect to the initial data. The proofs combine Lyapunov functions and Markov semigroups on weighted spaces with Kunita's theory of the differentiable dependence of SDE solutions on the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Artur Sidorenko, Vasilii Kolokoltsov

item.title: Finite-Sample Bounds for Fr\'echet Means of Dependent Data in Metric Spaces with Curvature Bounded Above
item.description: arXiv:2610.13362v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove finite-sample risk bounds for empirical quadratic and power Fr\'echet means in geodesic metric spaces with curvature bounded above for observations with arbitrary joint law. We compare the sample with exchangeable copies in which one observation is redrawn independently of the original sample and the others move to preserve the joint law. These displacements control the error, with no entropy or dimension assumptions. For quadratic Fr\'echet means, this yields a general ``coupling bound'' in any separable complete $CAT(\kappa)$ space, where for $\kappa>0$ the observations must lie in a closed convex set of circumradius below $\pi/(2\sqrt{\kappa})$. This bound is exact on the real line for nonnegatively correlated Gaussian observations and for comonotone functions of a common factor. We apply it in two settings. Under local dependence, the resulting risk bound grows linearly with the average size of the dependency neighborhoods. Under transport sensitivity and for bounded metric variances, summable sensitivities of the conditional laws to a change in one observation preserve the parametric mean squared error rate, while nonsummable polynomial decay gives explicit slower rates. We verify transport sensitivity for stationary reversible Markov chains with Wasserstein-contractive kernels and for bi-Lipschitz images of Gaussian sequences. In the more challenging setting of heavy-tailed, dependent data with possibly infinite variance, we consider power Fr\'echet means of order $\alpha\in(1,2)$. Under nonpositive curvature, we bound their $L^\alpha$ risk assuming only finite $\alpha$-th moments.
item.dc:creator: Zoraida F. Rico, Christof Sch\"otz

item.title: Utility-Based Recovery Risk Measures: Redundancy and Approximation for Portfolio Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.13454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recovery risk measures incorporate explicit liability-recovery requirements into asset-liability risk assessment. We study their specialization to optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), allowing the underlying utility specification to vary across recovery levels and encompassing Recovery Average Value at Risk (RecAV@R) as a special case. For finite recovery specifications, we use the dual penalty representation to characterize redundant recovery regimes and derive position-independent screening conditions. For a subfamily of the Cressie-Read power-divergence family, including entropic and truncated-quadratic specifications, we obtain an exact characterization on atomless probability spaces: universal redundancy is equivalent to a two-dimensional convex-hull condition involving recovery levels and divergence-scale parameters. On such spaces, universal redundancy for RecAV@R reduces to pairwise dominance, whereas for power-divergence OCEs it can arise from the joint effect of several recovery regimes. For nonlinear OCE utilities, we develop a certified piecewise-linear approximation framework for portfolio optimization. In finite-scenario models, the approximating problems are finite-dimensional linear programs, while utility approximation errors transfer directly to the Recovery OCE, yielding explicit error bounds and convergence rates. Uniform approximation over the portfolio domain further implies convergence of optimal values and stability of optimal solutions. A numerical asset-liability study illustrates the effects of recovery-dependent risk preferences and the accuracy and convergence of the approximation.
item.dc:creator: Justin Pl\"uckebaum, Stefan Weber

item.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
item.description: arXiv:2610.13505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semi-Markov networks provide a natural framework for describing stochastic transitions between coarse-grained states with non-exponential dwell times, with applications ranging from biophysics and neuroscience to epidemiology and finance. Here, it is shown that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph. These representations yield asymptotic results, including a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem to semi-Markov networks, in which the rate constants replaced by pseudo-rates given by the inverse mean sojourn time weighted by the exit probability through this channel, as well as the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short proof of the constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to show that weak ergodicity breaking occurs generically for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks.
item.dc:creator: Julian Voits

item.title: Stationary Ergodic Mean-field Games of Constrained Singular Controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.13544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a stationary ergodic mean-field game of scalar type where the representative player controls a diffusion through two-sided singular controls exerted only at the jump times of an independent Poisson process. For each mean-field parameter, we solve the novel constrained ergodic singular control problem, proving that the optimal policy is of threshold type: the diffusion is reset at Poisson arrival times to the nearest boundary point of an interval. Our explicit probabilistic derivation of the stationary distributions induced by Poissonian threshold singular controls is a key contribution of independent interest. This distribution is used to construct the mean-field fixed-point map. We prove existence and uniqueness of the stationary mean-field equilibrium by combining the stationary density with the monotonicity and continuity of the optimal thresholds in the mean-field parameter. The model provides a tractable framework for a case study of partially reversible investment with singular adjustments under exogenous intervention constraints.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Ferrari, Jukka Lempa, Neofytos Rodosthenous, Harto Saarinen

item.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,\lambda \in (0,1)$: \[ \gamma_{\Sigma_1}(K)^{1-p} \gamma_{\Sigma_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-\lambda} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}{\lambda} \right)^p \right)^{n} \gamma_{\Gamma}((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L) , \] whenever $\Gamma \leq \Sigma_1 \sharp_p \Sigma_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \Gamma$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=\lambda$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: \[ \gamma(a K)^{1-\lambda} \gamma(b L)^{\lambda} \leq \gamma \left ( a^{1-\lambda} b^\lambda \left ((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman, Shohei Nakamura, Hiroshi Tsuji

item.title: Critical Ising model as the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.13705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a linear map from the space of spin polynomials in the critical Ising model on a lattice to the state space of the $M(4,3)$ minimal model of conformal field theory. The kernel of the map consists precisely of null fields, i.e., spin polynomials that vanish in all correlations. For a polynomial $\Op$ which is not a null field, we define its scaling dimension $\Delta_{\Op}\in\Z_{\geq0}\cup(\Z_{\geq0}+\frac{1}{8}),$ to be the lowest $\Loper{0}+\Loperbar{0}$ eigenvalue in the decomposition of its image into homogeneous components. We show that as the mesh size $\delta$ goes to zero, the rescaled field $\delta^{-\Delta_{\Op}}\Op$ has a non-trivial scaling limit, when inserted in correlations with other such fields. Moreover, all these limits can be expressed in terms of correlations of primary fields of $M(4,3)$ and the Virasoro action in the continuum. The highest weight vectors of $M(4,3)$, the joint eigenvectors of $\Loper{0}$ and $\Loperbar{0}$ with the same eigenvalues $0,1/16,1/2$ for both, are the images of the constant $1$, the spin at a single lattice vertex, and the energy at a single lattice edge, respectively. For the proof, we construct a map from a larger lattice field space, accommodating also fermion and disorder insertions, to a direct sum of two fermionic Fock spaces. This direct sum contains contains the state spaces of both the $M(4,3)$ and the free fermion CFT. The main technical ingredient of the proof is a new version of the exact fermionic current action on the space of lattice local fields due to C. Hongler, K.K. and F. Viklund, combined with some new advances in discrete complex analysis. Our results are valid on arbitrary isoradial graphs.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Chelkak, Konstantin Izyurov, Kalle Kyt\"ol\"a

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).
item.dc:creator: Anumula Venkata Sai Sree Sahithi, Arti Yardi, Jithin Ravi

item.title: Large deviation principle at speed $n^d$ for the random metric in first-passage percolation
item.description: arXiv:2404.09589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the standard first passage percolation model on $\mathbb Z^d$ with bounded weights. We show a large deviation estimate for the probability that the rescaled passage time restricted to a box is greater than a target pseudometric. Moreover, the associated rate function can be written as the integral over the box of an elementary cost. Under the additional assumption that weights are bounded away from zero, the random pseudometric follows a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n^d$. Consequences include LDPs at speed $n^d$ for the point-to-point passage time, the crossing passage time and the random ball of radius $n$. Our strategy consists in proving first the existence of the rate function for any seminorm $g$ with a multidimensional subadditivity argument, then using this result as an elementary building block to estimate the rate function in full generality.
item.dc:creator: Julien Verges (Stockholm University)

item.title: On the Kantorovich contraction of Markov semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2511.08111v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an operator-theoretic framework for the contraction properties of Markov semigroups with respect to a general class of Kantorovich semi-distances, which includes Wasserstein distances and weighted total variation norms. The framework is based on Kantorovich contraction coefficients, which extend Dobrushin's ergodic coefficient from the total variation distance to general transport costs. Our main result shows that a geometric drift condition, combined with a local contraction condition on the sub-level sets of the Lyapunov function, implies that the Markov operator is a strict contraction with respect to an explicit modification of the underlying Kantorovich cost. This yields, in a unified way, the existence and uniqueness of invariant measures and exponential decay estimates in Wasserstein distances, for both discrete time and continuous time Markov semigroups, as well as for time-varying semigroups. We illustrate the scope of the framework with (i) Markov transitions on models with boundary states, including bounded domains with entrance boundaries, (ii) operator products of a Markov kernel and its adjoint, including two-block Gibbs samplers, (iii) iterated random functions, including Euler-type schemes, (iv) diffusion models, including overdamped Langevin diffusions with potentials that are convex at infinity, jump-diffusions on compact manifolds, and Jacobi and Riccati matrix diffusions, and (v) time-varying and nonlinear semigroups, including Feynman-Kac distribution flows and Sinkhorn bridges. In several of these settings we obtain new contraction estimates, while in others we recover known results through short and elementary arguments.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Del Moral, Mathieu Gerber

item.title: Sharpness of the percolation phase transition for weighted random connection models
item.description: arXiv:2512.21742v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the sharpness of the percolation phase transition for a class of potentially infinite-range weighted random connection models. The vertex set is given by a marked Poisson point process on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq 2$, with intensity $\lambda>0$, where each vertex carries an independent weight. Given a pair of vertices, an edge is drawn independently with a probability that depends on both their spatial displacement and their respective weights. Our geometric and moment assumptions allow the expected degree to be unbounded over the weights. We prove exponential tails for the number of vertices in the root cluster throughout the subcritical regime. We also obtain a linear lower bound on the percolation probability near criticality from above. The class of systems considered includes min-reach models, Poisson--Boolean overlap models, and suitable softened versions thereof. Our proof combines a finite-volume lattice approximation with Hutchcroft's exploration approach to the OSSS inequality.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Caicedo, Leonid Kolesnikov

item.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
item.description: arXiv:2601.14074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Arcia-Manoleskos, Manuel Dom\'inguez de la Iglesia

item.title: Fine asymptotics of the magnetization of the annealed dilute Curie-Weiss model
item.description: arXiv:2603.09672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the dilute Curie-Weiss model of size $N$, which is a generalization of the classical Curie-Weiss model in which the dependency structure between the spins is encoded not by the complete graph but by the (directed) Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph on $N$ vertices in which every edge appears independently with probability $p(N)$. In the high-temperature regime with an external magnetic field ($0<\beta<1,h\in\mathbb{R}$) we prove for $p^{3}N^{2}\to\infty$ sharp cumulant bounds for the magnetization under the annealed Gibbs measure, which imply a central limit theorem with rate, moderate and large deviation principles, a concentration inequality, a normal approximation with Cram\'er correction and mod-Gaussian convergence.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Apostel, Hanna D\"oring, Kristina Schubert

item.title: Strong invariance principles for diffusions, Markov chains and their perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.11142v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we construct strong approximations for discrete-time Markov chains weakly converging to continuous diffusion processes, as well as for their perturbed counterparts. Under the assumption of bounded coefficients, we construct closely coupled versions of these processes on a shared probability space. In particular, for both non-degenerate and degenerate cases, we maximize the probability of their exact pathwise coincidence on discrete time grids. Moreover, we construct such probability space that the probability of small deviation of the interpolated Markov chain from the continuous diffusion trajectory is small on the entire time interval if the perturbation is small enough.
item.dc:creator: V. Konakov, D. Kucher, E. Mammen

item.title: Spectrum of Directed Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.08696v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the spectrum of the adjacency matrix $A_n$ of directed inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices. We assume that $A_n$ has independent entries and diverging average degree scale $s_n$. This framework includes, as special cases, the directed Chung--Lu random graph and directed stochastic block models. Assuming boundedness of the variance profile and that $s_n$ diverges faster than $\log(n)^2$, we show that the rank-one Chung--Lu model satisfies a non-homogeneous version of the circular law, which in some situations allows for an explicit expression. Moreover, under mild conditions, we identify the asymptotic singular value distribution using tools from free probability. Finally, for finite-rank directed models, we establish that eigenvalues outside the bulk have joint Gaussian fluctuations at the scale $\sqrt{s_n/n}$, with an explicit covariance matrix. These results extend the theory of spectral outliers and their fluctuations to directed inhomogeneous random graphs.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Subhra Hazra, Giacomo Passuello

item.title: On the First Hitting Time Problems for Diffusion Processes: Local Time-Space Approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.13732v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the local time-space calculus of Peskir (2005) and the method developed in Mijatovic (2010), we derive a new integral representation for the backward probability associated with the first-passage time (FPT) of a diffusion process through a time-dependent barrier. We present a complete three-step numerical algorithm: first, the problem is reduced to a Volterra-type integral equation; second, its kernel is approximated by a Markov chain; finally, the resulting equation is solved using a quadrature rule. The method is implemented for several representative examples, and its convergence properties are established. An extension to double barrier problems is carried out
item.dc:creator: Jerome Detemple, Yerkin Kitapbayev, Danila Shabalin

item.title: Large deviations of the spectral radius of iid subgaussian random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.05498v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study large deviations of the spectral radius of $X_n=n^{-1/2}(\xi_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$, where the entries are iid, centered, variance-one, and subgaussian, with zero pseudovariance in the complex case. We write $\rho(X_n)$ for its spectral radius, i.e. the largest modulus among its eigenvalues. For every fixed $r>1$, we prove $$ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\mathbb{P}\{\rho(X_n)>r\} \ge -\frac\beta2\bigl(r^2-1-2\log r\bigr), $$ where $\beta=1$ for real entries and $\beta=2$ for complex entries. We prove a matching upper bound for real symmetric laws with Gaussian-dominated even moments and for complex laws satisfying the sharp Gaussian Laplace-transform bound. These classes include discrete distributions. In the complex sharp class, we also identify the exponential rate for an eigenvalue to enter a fixed disk outside the unit disk. We then turn to lower deviations and establish a quadratic-speed bound. Under the additional assumption that the entry law $\mu$ has a bounded density, we prove $$ \mathbb{P}\{\rho(X_n)\le r\}\le e^{-c_{\mu,r}n^2} $$ for every fixed $0<r<1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, where $c_{\mu,r}>0$. For the matching upper-tail classes with a bounded density, these bounds give a full speed-$n$ large deviation principle, with the displayed upper-tail rate for $r\ge1$ and infinite rate for $r<1$. The upper-tail proof uses a change of measure that preserves the entry support and creates an outlying eigenvalue. The lower-tail proof develops a weighted comparison for adaptive orthonormal observations and applies it to Arnoldi residuals.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Exact bounds on the distribution function of isotropic log-concave distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10289v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each real $b$, exact upper and lower bounds on the probability $\mathsf P(X\ge b)$ over all random variables $X$ with log-concave p.d.f.'s such that $\mathsf E X=0$ and $\mathsf E X^2=1$ are obtained, as well as the best constant factor $C$ in the inequality $\mathsf P(X\ge b)\le C e^{-b}$ for all real $b\ge0$. Exact upper and lower bounds on the corresponding exponential moments (Proposition 9.4) and explicit exponentially decreasing upper bounds on the mentioned p.d.f.'s (Propositions 9.2 and 9.3) are given as well. Some general results concerning log-concave p.d.f.'s are also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Pinelis

item.title: High order integration of stochastic dynamics on Riemannian manifolds with frozen flow methods
item.description: arXiv:2503.21855v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a new class of numerical methods for solving stochastic differential equations with additive noise on general Riemannian manifolds with high weak order of accuracy. In opposition to the popular approach with projection methods, the proposed methods are intrinsic: they only rely on geometric operations and avoid coordinates and embeddings. We provide a robust and general convergence analysis and an algebraic formalism of exotic planar Butcher series for the computation of order conditions at any high order. To illustrate the methodology, an explicit method of second weak order is introduced, and several numerical experiments confirm the theoretical findings and extend the approach for the sampling of the invariant measure of Riemannian Langevin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Eugen Bronasco, Adrien Busnot Laurent, Baptiste Huguet

item.title: A Unifying Framework for Global Optimization: From Theory to Formalization
item.description: arXiv:2508.20671v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce an abstract measure___theoretic framework that serves as a tool to rigorously study stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms as a unified class. The framework is formulated in terms of probability kernels, which, via the Ionescu--Tulcea theorem, induce probability measures on the space of sequences of algorithm iterations, endowed with two intuitive properties. This framework answers the need for a general, implementation___independent formalism in the analysis of such algorithms, providing a starting point for formalizing global optimization results in proof-assistants. To illustrate the relevance of our tool, we show that common algorithms fit naturally in the framework, and we also use it to give a rigorous proof of a general consistency theorem for stochastic iterative global optimization algorithms (Proposition 3 of (Malherbe, et al., 2017). This proof and the entire framework are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. This formalization both ensures the correctness of the definitions and proofs, and provides a basis for future machine-assisted formalizations in the field.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Serr\'e (ENS Paris Saclay, CB), Argyris Kalogeratos (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), Nicolas Vayatis (CB, ENS Paris Saclay)

item.title: Why does entropy drive evolution equations?
item.description: arXiv:2603.07653v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: `Entropy' appears as driving force in many different evolution equations, both deterministic and stochastic, and in these equations this `entropy' also takes different forms. We show how all these examples can be understood as different instances of a common principle: Entropy drives evolutions because it characterizes the invariant measure of an underlying stochastic process. This interpretation explains the appearance of entropy, the different forms that entropy takes in these equations, and how entropy `drives' these evolution equations. We illustrate this common structure with examples from stochastic processes, gradient flows, and GENERIC systems.
item.dc:creator: Mark A. Peletier

item.title: Nonlocal Characterizations of Stochastic Completeness on Complete Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.20205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we first prove that the following generalized conservation principle holds on complete Riemannian manifolds: for every \(0<s<1\) and \(t>0\), \[ T_t^{(s)}\mathbf 1+\int_0^t T_\tau^{(s)}\mathcal R_s\,d\tau=1 \qquad\text{on }M, \] where \(\mathcal R_s\) is the intrinsic killing term measuring the loss of mass of the subordinate semigroup, and the condition \(\mathcal R_s\equiv0\) is equivalent to the stochastic completeness of \(M\). We then provide several new nonlocal characterizations of stochastic completeness. In particular, we show that stochastic completeness is equivalent to genuinely nonlocal conditions, including the zero-mean identity \[ \int_M (-\Delta)^s\varphi\,dV_g=0 \qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(M), \] as well as the uniqueness of bounded distributional solutions to the associated fractional elliptic and parabolic equations. We also revisit the equivalent \(L^1\)-core characterization for the generator of the heat semigroup, which plays an important role in our approach. In addition, we prove \(L^p\)-contractivity and smoothing properties of the subordinate semigroup, establish both short-time and long-time asymptotic results for the fractional heat kernel, derive the short-time asymptotics of jump probabilities for the associated Markov process, and study the variational characterization and minimality properties of the fractional resolvent. Together, these results provide a unified analytic and probabilistic framework for the fractional Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Rui Chen, Bobo Hua

item.title: Stochastic Policy Gradient Methods in the Uncertain Volatility Model
item.description: arXiv:2605.06670v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The multidimensional Uncertain Volatility Model leads to robust option pricing problems under joint volatility and correlation uncertainty. Their numerical resolution quickly becomes challenging because the associated stochastic control problem is high-dimensional. We propose a backward actor-critic stochastic policy-gradient scheme tailored to this setting. The method combines a discrete dynamic programming principle with Proximal Policy Optimization and one-hidden-layer neural-network approximations of both the value function and the control policy. A key ingredient is the policy parameterization: continuous controls are represented through a squashed Gaussian policy built on a $C$-vine representation of correlation matrices, which enforces positive definiteness by construction. Beyond the robust price itself, the spatial gradient of the trained critic provides an approximation of the associated superhedging strategy. We assess the quality of this learned gradient through a dual formulation, which also yields a numerical dual estimate of the price. Numerical experiments on a range of multidimensional derivatives show that the method yields accurate prices, remains computationally efficient, and compares favorably with existing Monte Carlo and machine-learning-based benchmarks for robust pricing in the Uncertain Volatility Model.
item.dc:creator: Lokman A Abbas-Turki (LPSM), Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Chassagneux (ENSAE Paris), Jean-Philippe Lemor (LPSM), Gr\'egoire Loeper (LPSM), Simon Sananes (LPSM)

item.title: Universality in the target arrival statistics of non-conservative search processes
item.description: arXiv:2606.16025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic search processes in which agents are continuously inserted into and removed from a target search domain are fundamental to a wide class of physical and artificial systems. The theory of such non-conservative search processes is, however, much less developed than for search processes with a fixed number of agents. Recent work on the non-conservative case has characterized the fastest first-passage time (FPT) to a target, after which the search process is terminated. Here we consider the complementary problem of continuous arrival statistics to a target. In particular, we derive the full time-dependent distribution of target arrivals, which we use to show that the inter-arrival time distribution is exactly exponential in steady-state regardless of the underlying search process. Thus, counterintuitively, the arrival statistics of non-conservative search are both universal and much simpler than sequential search-and-capture processes involving a fixed number of agents. Our methods also yield an exact expression for the fastest FPT distribution with time-dependent insertion, thereby generalizing previous work on fixed-rate insertion for non-conservative search. Altogether these results have major implications for target resource accumulation, wherein the delivery of resources is counter-balanced by their downstream consumption.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Giral-Barajas, Samantha Linn, Paul C. Bressloff

item.title: Dense alternating sign matrices and imprecise copulas
item.description: arXiv:2607.06178v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study discrete quasi-copulas and discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range, which naturally correspond to alternating sign matrices. We identify dense alternating sign matrices as a particularly well-behaved subclass. We prove that the associated discrete imprecise copulas are always coherent and hence avoid sure loss. We further show that a particular extension of the corresponding discrete quasi-copulas to the full domain preserves this structure and yields self-dual imprecise copulas. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first general result in the literature showing how properties established for discrete imprecise copulas can be preserved when extending them to their full-domain counterpart. We conclude the paper by showing that, for general alternating sign matrices, the associated discrete imprecise copulas need not avoid sure loss, further emphasizing the special role of the subclass of dense alternating sign matrices. We establish, however, that the class of discrete quasi-copulas of minimal range is invariant under all defect transformations
item.dc:creator: Toma\v{z} Ko\v{s}ir, Elisa Perrone, Nik Stopar

item.title: $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)_2$ Theory from many-body quantum Gibbs states
item.description: arXiv:2607.23084v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive the $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)_2$ measure on the two-dimensional unit torus as the rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states. In particular, the quantum model corresponding to the $\Phi^{2p}_2$ measure is formulated in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric $p$-body interaction potential which is not required to have a factorized form. Unlike in the $\Phi^4_2$ case investigated by Fr\"ohlich--Knowles--Schlein--Sohinger in \cite{FKSS25}, in the treatment of higher-order interactions, Wick renormalization generates a full hierarchy of lower-order interactions which we organize systematically using a graphical formalism. One key ingredient of our analysis is a logarithmic stability estimate for both the nonlocal Hartree functional and the many-body Hamiltonian that is uniform in the interaction range, allowing us to use the positivity of the leading $p$-body interaction to control all lower-order terms generated by the Wick counterterms.
item.dc:creator: Phan Th\`anh Nam, Zhilin Yang, Xiangchan Zhu

item.title: Dynamical classical-field limit of Bosonic Gibbs states: Renormalized Hartree NLS correlations in 2D and 3D
item.description: arXiv:2608.26477v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we derive the time-dependent correlation functions of the renormalized Hartree NLS equation on the torus $\mathbb T^d$, $d=2,3$, from the corresponding bosonic many-body Gibbs dynamics. In contrast with the 1D problem studied earlier by Fr\"ohlich, Knowles, Schlein and Sohinger, in higher dimensions the scaled quantum particle number is not uniformly bounded and the relevant classical fields require Wick renormalization. Our proof combines convergence of the quantum generators in weighted Hilbert spaces with uniqueness for positive solutions of the limiting Liouville equation that are dominated by the Gibbs measure.
item.dc:creator: Phan Th\`anh Nam, Rongchan Zhu, Xiangchan Zhu

item.title: Robust LassoNet: Enhancing Feature Selection in Neural Networks via Robust Loss Functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.38263v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Feature selection in neural networks remains a challenging problem, particularly in the presence of noisy or contaminated data. LassoNet is a recent approach that addresses this issue by combining neural networks with hierarchical sparsity constraints, enabling simultaneous prediction and variable selection. However, its standard formulation relies on the mean squared error (MSE) loss, which is known to be highly sensitive to outliers. In this paper, we present Robust LassoNet, an extension of LassoNet that incorporates robust loss functions, such as Huber, Cauchy, Tukey's bisquare, and Nonnegative Garrote, to mitigate the effect of extreme observations. The proposed approach preserves the original optimization framework while improving stability under data contamination. Through experiments on synthetic and real datasets, we show that robust LassoNet significantly improves both predictive performance and feature selection accuracy in the presence of outliers or heavy tailed noise, while maintaining comparable performance in clean settings. These results highlight the importance of robustness in neural network based feature selection and suggest practical guidelines for choosing appropriate loss functions.
item.dc:creator: Daniela De Canditiis, Italia De Feis, Paola Stolfi
